summary: This packet decomposes the arithmetic fundamental group and inverse Galois programme from five authorized public sources, none in the supplied library: SGA 1 (arXiv reprint of the SMF 2003 edition), Debes, Arithmetique des revetements de la droite (lecture notes, 2024 author copy), Neukirch-Schmidt-Wingberg, Cohomology of Number Fields (electronic edition 2.3, free for non-commercial use), Romagny-Wewers, Hurwitz spaces (Seminaires et Congres 13, author copy), and Debes, Hurwitz spaces and Inverse Galois Theory (arXiv 2601.06532v2). IG.0 covers Galois categories (SGA 1 V 4.1), fibre functors and exact functors, pi_1 of schemes and fields. IG.1 covers the fundamental exact sequence and its splitting, homotopy sequences for proper morphisms, specialization with prime-to-p control, tame pi_1 of punctured curves and pi_1(G_m) in characteristic 0 (the IG.0 acceptance check, placed after IG.1). IG.2 covers Hilbertian fields, the Hilbert-Dorge proof for Q, finite extensions and specialization of Galois extensions. IG.3 covers Riemann existence, the descent criterion with branch cycle conditions, rigidity with S_n and PSL_2(F_p), fields of moduli and real realizations. IG.4 covers embedding problems and Shafarevich's theorem via NSW 9.6. IG.5 covers Hurwitz spaces over Z, braid components, and the tame-only characteristic-p statements. IG.6 is a theorem-indexed register with the inverse Galois problem over Q open. All stages remain partial: Riemann existence and Hurwitz-space proofs, decomposition and inertia groups, the shrinking process, Belyi supplier checks and the worked certified examples are unread or absent.

nodes.title: SGA 1 V Theoreme 4.1: a category with (G1)-(G3) and a fibre functor with (G4)-(G6) is equivalent to finite continuous pi-sets
nodes.statement: Let C be a category and F a covariant functor from C to finite sets such that (G1) C has a final object and fibre products; (G2) C has finite sums and quotients by finite groups of automorphisms; (G3) every morphism factors as a strict epimorphism followed by a monomorphism that is an isomorphism onto a direct summand; (G4) F is left exact; (G5) F commutes with finite sums, sends strict epimorphisms to epimorphisms and commutes with quotients by finite groups; (G6) F reflects isomorphisms. Then F is pro-representable by a pro-object P = (P_i) of C with epimorphic transition maps, the Galois P_i are cofinal, Aut(P) = lim Aut(P_i) is profinite, and with pi the group opposite to Aut(P), F : C -> C(pi) and G(E) = P x^pi E are quasi-inverse equivalences, where C(pi) is the category of finite sets with continuous left pi-action. A category equivalent to some C(pi) is a Galois category, and a functor satisfying (G4)-(G6) is a fundamental (fibre) functor.
hypotheses: Imported: strict pro-representability of a left exact functor on a category whose objects are artinian (Grothendieck, Technique de descente II, Seminaire Bourbaki 195, prop. 3.1), used in step c)
Remarques 4.2: (G2) and (G5) may be replaced by the stronger-looking finite colimits and right exactness, which follow from the theorem
Step m) is dismissed as "Ane qui trotte" (routine verification)
proofSteps: a) u is a monomorphism iff F(u) is (G1, G4, G6); b) every object is artinian.
c) F is strictly pro-representable: F(X) = lim Hom(P_i, X) with epimorphic transition maps (imported criterion).
d) The P_i are connected and not initial; e) morphisms from a nonempty object to a connected object are strict epimorphisms, and endomorphisms of connected objects are automorphisms.
f) Aut(P_i) acts transitively on F(P_i) iff simply transitively (Galois objects); g) every X is dominated by a Galois P_i, so Galois objects are cofinal.
h) Aut(P) = lim Aut(P_i) = lim F(P_i), a profinite group; pi (opposite group) acts continuously on F(X) = Hom(P, X).
i)-k) Construct G(E) = P x^pi E as P_i x^{pi_i} E for pi_i acting on E, using quotients by finite groups (G2, G5).
l)-n) The natural maps alpha : id -> FG and beta : GF -> id are isomorphisms.
acceptance: Recover C(pi) itself: the canonical forgetful functor on finite continuous pi-sets satisfies (G1)-(G6), with pro-object the system of finite quotients of pi.
Check the import in step c) against a supplier proof (e.g. an elementary proof of the main theorem on Galois categories).

nodes.title: SGA 1 V 5.3-5.7 and 6.1-6.13: connected objects, the fundamental groupoid, base-point change, and the dictionary between exact functors and continuous homomorphisms
nodes.statement: Let C be a Galois category with fibre functor F and pi = Aut(F). (5.3-5.4) X is connected iff pi acts transitively on F(X), and a nonempty connected X is isomorphic to some P_i. (5.7) Any two fibre functors are isomorphic, so the fibre functors form a connected groupoid whose automorphism groups are isomorphic to pi, the isomorphism being determined up to inner automorphism; Isom(F, F') plays the role of path classes. (6.1-6.2) A functor H : C -> C' between Galois categories is exact iff F' o H is a fibre functor, and then H corresponds to a continuous homomorphism u : pi_{F'} -> pi_F. (6.4) For a pointed connected X with open stabilizer U, U contains u(pi_{F'}) iff H(X) has a pointed section. (6.9) u is surjective iff H preserves connected objects iff H is fully faithful; (6.10) u is an isomorphism iff H is an equivalence. (6.13) For connected S in C and a in F(S), C/S is Galois and pi of the fibre over a is the open stabilizer of a.
hypotheses: Proposition 6.13 is stated with "La demonstration est laissee au lecteur"
Proposition 6.11 gives the criteria for Ker u contained in Im u' and the converse used for exact sequences of fundamental groups
proofSteps: 5.3: reduce to C = C(pi), where connected objects are transitive pi-sets.
5.5-5.6: a pro-object Q defines a functor commuting with finite sums iff Q = pi/H for a closed subgroup H; it is fundamental iff H = 1.
5.7: any two fundamental pro-objects are isomorphic; Aut(F) = pi up to inner automorphism.
6.1: exactness of H is equivalent to F' o H being fundamental (5.6); the induced map of automorphism groups is continuous because finite pi_F-sets pull back to continuous pi_{F'}-sets.
6.4-6.13: translate properties of H into properties of u using pointed connected objects = open subgroups.
acceptance: Base-point change: record the inner-automorphism ambiguity explicitly when comparing pi_1 at two geometric points.
Use 6.9 and 6.11 as the dictionary for the exact sequences of IG.1.

nodes.title: SGA 1 V section 7: for a connected locally noetherian scheme S and a geometric point a, finite etale covers with the geometric-fibre functor form a Galois category with group pi_1(S, a)
nodes.statement: Let S be a connected locally noetherian scheme and a : Spec(Omega) -> S a geometric point. The category C of finite etale covers of S with F(X) = geometric points of X over a satisfies (G1)-(G6). Hence there is a universal cover (pro-object) P at a and a profinite group pi_1(S, a) = Aut(F) with C equivalent to finite continuous pi_1(S, a)-sets. A cover is connected iff pi_1 acts transitively on its fibre. For another geometric point a' (possibly in another characteristic) the fibre functors are isomorphic, giving the groupoid of path classes pi_1(S; a, a'). A morphism f : S' -> S induces pi_1(f; a') : pi_1(S', a') -> pi_1(S, f(a')), and for a finite etale connected S' this is an isomorphism onto the open stabilizer of a'.
hypotheses: (G1) from I 4.6, (G2) from V 3.4, (G3) and (G5) from V 3.5 and section 2, (G6) from V 3.7: these facts about etale covers (Exposes I and V sections 1-3) were not read
Principal covers with group G correspond to principal homogeneous objects in C (via criterion V 2.6(iii), not read)
Non-connected S: multi-Galois categories (section 9), sketched only
proofSteps: Verify (G1)-(G6) for finite etale covers using the cited results of Exposes I and V.
Apply Theoreme 4.1 to get P and pi_1(S, a), and 5.7 for independence of a.
Apply the dictionary of section 6 to the pullback functor f^*.

nodes.title: SGA 1 V Propositions 8.1-8.2: pi_1(Spec k) is the absolute Galois group, and pi_1 of a normal connected scheme is Gal(K^s/K) modulo the subgroup fixing the unramified extensions
nodes.statement: For a field k and an algebraically closed extension Omega defining a geometric point a of S = Spec k, with k^s the separable closure of k in Omega, there is a canonical isomorphism pi_1(S, a) = Gal(k^s/k). If S is a connected locally noetherian normal scheme with function field K and Omega an algebraically closed extension of K, then pi_1(Spec K) -> pi_1(S) is surjective, and its kernel corresponds, by Galois theory, to the compositum of the finite subextensions of K^s/K that are unramified over S.
hypotheses: 8.2 uses I 10.1 (a connected etale cover of a normal scheme is integral), not read
proofSteps: 8.1: a finite etale cover of Spec k is Spec of a finite separable algebra; k-embeddings into Omega land in k^s; the Galois group of k^s/k acts on fibres, giving a homomorphism to pi_1 that is injective (an automorphism trivial on all finite separable subextensions is trivial) and surjective (transitivity on embeddings of a finite separable L).
8.2: surjectivity means pullbacks of connected etale covers to Spec K are connected (X integral); the kernel consists of automorphisms acting trivially on all finite subextensions unramified over S.
acceptance: IG.0 acceptance: recover the absolute Galois group for Spec K.

nodes.title: SGA 1 XIII Corollaire 2.12 in genus 0 with two points, via XII 5.2: pi_1 of G_m over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field is Zhat
nodes.statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 and U = P^1_k minus {0, infinity} = G_m. By SGA 1 XIII Corollaire 2.12 with g = 0 and n = 2, pi_1(U) = pi_1^t(U) is generated by two inertia generators sigma_1, sigma_2 with sigma_1 sigma_2 = 1, and in characteristic 0 (p' = all primes) it is the profinite group with this presentation, hence isomorphic to Zhat; each quotient Z/nZ corresponds to the Kummer cover t -> t^n. For k = C this is the profinite completion of pi_1^top(C^*) = Z by XII Corollaire 5.2.
hypotheses: Corollaire 2.12 in characteristic 0 is proved by descending to a subfield of finite transcendence degree over Q, embedding into C, comparing via specialization isomorphisms of R^1 g_* (XIII 2.9, not read), and applying Riemann existence (XII 5.2)

nodes.title: SGA 1 IX Theoreme 6.1 and Corollaires 6.2, 6.4: 1 -> pi_1(Xbar_0) -> pi_1(X) -> Gal(kbar/k) -> 1 for quasi-compact geometrically connected X, split by a rational point
nodes.statement: Let S = Spec A with A artinian with residue field k, X an S-scheme with X_0 = X (x)_A k quasi-compact and geometrically connected over k, and Xbar_0 = X (x)_A kbar. Then e -> pi_1(Xbar_0, abar) -> pi_1(X, a) -> pi_1(S, b) -> e is exact, with pi_1(S, b) = Gal(kbar/k). Right exactness means (6.2) that an etale cover X' of X is of the form X x_S S' for S' etale over S iff its pullback to Xbar_0 is completely decomposed (for connected X': iff it has a section). If the geometric point is localized at a k-rational point (or one with radicial residue field), the sequence splits (6.4). The algebraic closure kbar cannot be replaced by an arbitrary algebraically closed extension in characteristic p (affine line, 6.3).
hypotheses: Left to the reader in the proof: pi_1(Xbar_0) = lim pi_1(X_i) over finite Galois subextensions k_i (limit argument)
Uses IX 3.4 (full faithfulness of pullback of etale covers), IX 4.11 (radicial extensions) and V 6.13, not all read

For finite Galois k_i/k with group pi_i, X_i = X (x)_k k_i is a connected principal cover of X with group pi_i (3.4), so V 6.13 gives e -> pi_1(X_i) -> pi_1(X) -> pi_i -> e.
Pass to the projective limit over i, using pi_1(Xbar_0) = lim pi_1(X_i).
6.4: a rational point gives a section S -> X and hence a splitting pi_1(S) -> pi_1(X).

nodes.title: Debes Theoreme 6.2.1: 1 -> pi_1(P^1 - t)_{k^s} -> pi_1(P^1 - t)_k -> G_k -> 1 splits, with a section s_{t0} for each unramified rational point
nodes.statement: Let k be a field and t = {t_1, ..., t_r} a Galois-stable set of points of P^1 (coordinates separable over k). Let Omega_t be the maximal separable extension of k^s(T) unramified above P^1 - t; then pi_1(P^1 - t)_{k^s} = Gal(Omega_t/k^s(T)) and pi_1(P^1 - t)_k = Gal(Omega_t/k(T)) fit into an exact sequence 1 -> pi_1(P^1 - t)_{k^s} -> pi_1(P^1 - t)_k -> G_k -> 1, which is split. For each unramified rational point t_0 in P^1(k) - t, the embedding Omega_t into k^s((T - t_0)) gives a section s_{t0}; in characteristic 0 a ramified rational point also gives a section via Puiseux series; if char k = p and P^1(k) is contained in t, then k = F_q and a lift of Frobenius gives a section. The section is well defined up to an element of pi_1(P^1 - t)_{k^s}.
hypotheses: The fundamental groups here are Galois groups of maximal unramified extensions of function fields; their identification with SGA 1 etale fundamental groups is not stated in the section read

Define s_{t0}(tau) = i^{-1} o tau-tilde o i, where tau-tilde acts on coefficients.
Finite field with every rational point in t: G_k is procyclic generated by Frobenius, and a lift gives the section.

nodes.statement: Let f : X -> Y be proper and separable (flat with geometrically reduced fibres) with Y locally noetherian and connected and f_*O_X = O_Y. For a geometric fibre Xbar_y, pi_1(Xbar_y, abar) -> pi_1(X, a) -> pi_1(Y, b) -> e is exact (1.4). For X proper connected and Y locally noetherian connected over an algebraically closed k, pi_1(X x_k Y) = pi_1(X) x pi_1(Y) (1.7), and for X proper connected over k and an algebraically closed extension k', pi_1(X (x)_k k') -> pi_1(X) is an isomorphism (1.8). Without properness these fail in characteristic p: the Artin-Schreier covers x^p - x = st of the affine line, parametrized by s, are etale and pairwise non-isomorphic (1.10).

nodes.title: SGA 1 X 2.1-2.12 and 3.8-3.10: surjective specialization maps for proper separable families, isomorphism on prime-to-p quotients for proper smooth families, and pi_1 of curves
nodes.statement: For Y the spectrum of a complete noetherian local ring and X proper over Y, pi_1(X_0) -> pi_1(X) is an isomorphism (2.1). For f : X -> Y proper with geometrically connected fibres, Y locally noetherian and y_0 in the closure of y_1, there is a specialization homomorphism pi_1(Xbar_1) -> pi_1(Xbar_0), defined up to inner automorphism, which is surjective if f is separable (2.3-2.4). If f is proper and smooth, every continuous homomorphism from pi_1(Xbar_1) to a finite group of order prime to p = char k(y_0) factors through pi_1(Xbar_0) (3.8); hence the specialization map is an isomorphism in characteristic 0 and induces an isomorphism of maximal prime-to-p quotients in characteristic p (3.9). For a proper smooth connected curve of genus g over an algebraically closed field, pi_1 has 2g topological generators with the surface relation, is the free profinite group on them with that relation in characteristic 0 (2.6), and its prime-to-p quotient has that presentation in characteristic p (3.10). The fundamental group of a proper connected scheme over an algebraically closed field is topologically finitely generated (2.9), so it has finitely many principal covers with a given finite group (2.12, Lang-Serre).
hypotheses: 2.1 is the formal existence theorem (EGA III, IX 1.10) in the language of fundamental groups: an import

2.6 and 3.10 are proved "par voie transcendante": comparison with the topological fundamental group of a compact orientable surface, whose derivation was "explicitee dans un des exposes oraux qui n'ont pas ete rediges"
3.8 uses purity (Zariski-Nagata, in the two-dimensional unequal characteristic case) and Abhyankar's lemma
Remarque 2.5: surjectivity fails without separability; Remarque 2.7: no purely algebraic proof of 2.6 is known (for g >= 2)
proofSteps: 2.2: combine 2.1 with IX 6.1 to get e -> pi_1(Xbar_0) -> pi_1(X) -> pi_1(Y) -> e with injective left map.
Define specialization by path classes from a_1 to a_0 and the isomorphisms pi_1(X_0) = pi_1(X), pi_1(k) = pi_1(Y); surjectivity follows when the generic sequence 1.4 is also exact.
3.8: for G of order prime to p, extend the Kummer-adjusted cover over the normal models using purity and Abhyankar's lemma.
2.9: induction on dimension via Chow's lemma, normalization and Bertini/Zariski connectedness for hyperplane sections (2.10-2.11).

nodes.title: SGA 1 XIII Lemme 2.11 and Corollaire 2.12: pi_1^t of a punctured curve is generated by 2g + n elements with inertia generators and one relation; its prime-to-p quotient is the pro-p' group with that presentation
nodes.statement: Let X be a proper smooth connected curve of genus g over a separably closed field k of characteristic p >= 0 and U = X minus n distinct closed points a_1, ..., a_n. The tamely ramified fundamental group pi_1^t(U) can be generated by 2g + n elements x_i, y_i, sigma_j with sigma_j generating an inertia group at a_j and prod_i [x_i, y_i] prod_j sigma_j = 1. For every finite group G of order prime to p generated by elements satisfying this relation there is an etale cover of U with group G realizing them; equivalently, pi_1^{p'}(U) is the pro-p' group with these generators and this single relation. Specialization maps carry inertia subgroups of pi_1^t to inertia subgroups (2.11).

In characteristic p the full pi_1(U) is not described: wild ramification contributes a large non-finitely-generated part for affine curves (IX 6.3, X 1.10)

nodes.title: Debes Definition 5.2.2: Hilbertian subsets H_{P_1..P_n} of k^r and Hilbertian fields; equivalence with the thin-set definition
nodes.statement: For a field k, integers r, s > 0 and polynomials P_1, ..., P_n in k(T_1, ..., T_r)[Y_1, ..., Y_s] irreducible over k(T), the Hilbertian subset H_{P_1..P_n} is the set of t in k^r such that each P_i(t, Y) is irreducible in k[Y]. The field k is Hilbertian if for every r > 0 the Hilbertian subsets of k^r are Zariski-dense (for r = 1: infinite). Equivalently (Remark 5.2.3, [Ser97], [Ser92]): k^r is not thin for every r > 0, thin sets being those contained in complements of Hilbertian subsets.

nodes.title: Debes Theoremes 5.2.4 and 5.2.9: Q is Hilbertian; the integers of a Hilbertian subset of Q have complement of size O(B^{1-delta}) in [1, B]
nodes.statement: For every Hilbertian subset H of Q there is delta > 0 such that the number of integers in [1, B] not in H is O(B^{1-delta}); in particular Q is Hilbertian and every Hilbertian subset of Q contains infinitely many primes. The proof, given for one parameter and one variable, reduces irreducibility of specializations to the absence of rational roots of finitely many monic, absolutely irreducible polynomials Q_i(T, Y) with no root in Q(T) (Proposition 5.2.5, Lemma 5.2.7), and bounds integer points on the real branches of such curves by Puiseux expansions and a Rolle interpolation argument (Lemmas 5.2.11-5.2.13).
hypotheses: Imported: the Puiseux theorem (Theoreme 6.1.1) and Corollaire 2.4.4 on primitive elements for unramified extensions (for convergence of Puiseux series, Lemma 5.2.12), neither read

The general case (several parameters and variables) follows from the reductions of section 9.1, not read beyond its opening; number fields and finitely generated extensions of Q are Hilbertian by Theoreme 9.2.1 and section 9.3
Lemma 5.2.7 has a characteristic-0 argument and a general argument through the field of constants (Proposition 5.3.2, not read)
Remark 5.2.10: the bound O(sqrt B) is possible ([Lan83], [Deb01]); the prime-number count uses the prime number theorem
proofSteps: Proposition 5.2.5: for an irreducible P, every nontrivial factorization of P(t_0, Y) comes from a subset I of the roots; a coefficient gamma of the corresponding factor lies outside k(T), and its minimal polynomial Q(T, Y) has a root at t_0; taking all I gives finitely many Q_i with V'_{Q_1..Q_N} contained in H_P up to a finite set.
Lemma 5.2.7: a separable irreducible but not absolutely irreducible Q has only finitely many k-rational zeros (they lie on the discriminant).
Lemma 5.2.11: the real branches of P(t, Y) = 0 for t large are given by convergent Puiseux series phi_i in (1/t)^{1/e} with real coefficients.

Lemma 5.2.13: for n + 1 integer points t_0 < ... < t_n on a branch with integer values, the n-th divided difference is a nonzero rational with denominator < (t_n - t_0)^{n(n+1)/2} but of size about t_0^{-mu}; so t_n - t_0 >= c t_0^alpha, and counting in intervals gives O(B^kappa) with kappa = 1/(1 + alpha).
Combine over the finitely many branches and polynomials.
acceptance: IG.2 acceptance support: the worked reduction for P(T, Y) = Y^4 - T (Exemple 5.2.6) gives explicit polynomials Q_1 = Y^4 - T, Q_2 = Y^2 - T, Q_3 = Y^2 + T whose rational-root-free values certify irreducibility.

nodes.title: Debes Proposition 5.2.14 and Remarque 5.2.15: over a Hilbertian field, a Galois extension of k(T) with group G specializes to Galois extensions of k with group G for infinitely many t
nodes.statement: Let k be a Hilbertian field and E_T/k(T) a Galois extension with group G, with primitive element y(T) integral over k[T] and monic minimal polynomial P(T, Y). For all t in the Hilbertian subset H_P outside a finite set (poles of the coefficients expressing the conjugates, zeros of the discriminant), the residue extension E_t = k(y(t)) is Galois over k with group isomorphic to G. The map s : Gal(E_t/k) -> Gal(E_T/k(T)) (extending tau to coefficients of the Hensel lifts in k((T - t))) is an isomorphism, and specialization of automorphisms r : Gal(E_T/k(T)) -> Gal(E_t/k) is a surjection with r o s = id. Hence a group realized over k(T) is realized over k.
hypotheses: Uses Hensel's lemma for the simple roots (Theoreme 1.3.12 or Lemme 2.6.4) and Lemme 1.4.2 (extension of the specialization morphism), not read

The regular-cover specialization "outside its branch locus" is covered by excluding discriminant zeros; the geometric formulation through decomposition groups (section 2.6, theoremes 2.6.1-2.6.2) was not read

For t in H_P outside the finitely many bad values, P(t, Y) is irreducible and splits as prod (Y - f_i(t, y(t))) with distinct roots, so E_t/k is Galois.
Identify E_T with k(T, y_1(T), ..., y_d(T)) inside k((T - t)) via Hensel lifts of the simple roots y_i(t), whose coefficients lie in E_t.
Extend tau in Gal(E_t/k) to coefficients; this preserves E_T and gives an injective homomorphism s; equality of orders ([E_t : k] = d = |G|) makes it an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Riemann existence: equivalences between finite extensions of C(T) unramified outside t, algebraic, analytic and topological covers, transitive representations of pi_1^top and permutation tuples with product one; Nielsen classes for G-covers
nodes.statement: For t = {t_1, ..., t_r} in P^1(C) the following categories are equivalent: finite extensions of C(T) unramified outside t; finite algebraic covers of P^1 unramified outside t; analytic covers of P^1(C) unramified outside t; finite topological covers of P^1(C) - t; transitive representations of pi_1^top(P^1(C) - t) in symmetric groups; r-tuples of permutations with product 1 generating a transitive subgroup (Debes Theoreme 6.5.1). Branch-cycle classes correspond to inertia canonical invariants (Proposition 6.5.2). For a finite group G, isomorphism classes of G-covers of P^1_C with branch locus D correspond bijectively to inner Nielsen classes ni_r(G) = {(g_1, ..., g_r) : g_i != 1, <g_i> = G, g_1 ... g_r = 1}/G (Romagny-Wewers Theorem 3.1). For an algebraically closed field k of characteristic 0, a bouquet gives i : pi_1^top(P^1 - t, t_0) -> pi_1^alg(P^1 - t)_k inducing an isomorphism from the profinite completion and sending [gamma_i] to a distinguished generator of an inertia group above t_i (Debes Theoreme 6.5.3). In SGA 1 form: for X locally of finite type over C, X' -> X'^an is an equivalence of finite etale covers (XII Theoreme 5.1).

nodes.title: Debes Theoremes 8.1.1-8.1.2 and conditions (*), (**), (***): a cover over k^s(T) is defined over k iff its representation extends to pi_1(P^1 - t)_k; the Galois action on branch cycles is twisted by the cyclotomic character
nodes.statement: Let E/F(T) be a (G-)extension unramified outside t, F/k Galois, with associated homomorphism phi : pi_1(P^1 - t)_F -> R (R = S_d or G). It is defined over k iff phi extends to pi_1(P^1 - t)_k (8.1.1). For F = k^s and a section s of 1 -> pi_1(P^1 - t)_{k^s} -> pi_1(P^1 - t)_k -> G_k -> 1, it is defined over k iff there is a homomorphism varphi : G_k -> R with phi(x^{s(tau)}) = varphi(tau) phi(x) varphi(tau)^{-1} for all tau and x (8.1.2). In characteristic 0, with a bouquet x_1, ..., x_r and g_i = phi(x_i): (*) the phi(x_i^{s(tau)}) generate G; (**) their product is 1; (***) phi(x_i^{s(tau)}) lies in C_j^{chi(tau)}, where t_j = t_i^tau, C_j is the inertia class at t_j and chi is the cyclotomic character modulo |G| (up to the normalizer for embedded classes). If varphi exists it takes values in N = Nor_R(G) and is determined modulo C = Cen_R(G) (8.1.3).

(*)-(***): the images of the conjugated bouquet again generate, have product 1, and represent the inertia classes twisted by the cyclotomic character.

nodes.title: Debes Theoreme 8.2.2 (Belyi, Fried, Matzat, Shih, Thompson): trivial center, rational classes and a transitive action on the Nielsen set give a regular G-extension of Q(T) with prescribed branch points
nodes.statement: Let G be a finite group with generators g_1, ..., g_r, g_1 ... g_r = 1, and conjugacy classes C_i of g_i. Let sni(C_1, ..., C_r) be the set of tuples (g'_1, ..., g'_r) generating G with product 1 and g'_i in C_i, with G acting by conjugation. If (H1) Z(G) = 1, (H2) the classes C_i are rational (g^a in C for all a prime to the order of g), and (H3) sni(C_1, ..., C_r) is nonempty and G acts transitively on it, then for every r-tuple t of points of P^1(Q) there is a regular Galois extension E/Q(T) with group G, branch points t and inertia canonical invariant (C_1, ..., C_r). Over Q^ab, (H2) is not needed (8.2.4); (H1) can be dropped using projectivity of G_{Q^ab} (8.2.5). (H2) is necessary when the t_i are rational (8.2.3).
hypotheses: (H3) is the rigidity condition; it is usually verified for r <= 3 and can be checked from character tables (8.2.2.3)
The proof uses the descent criterion 8.1.2 and conditions (*)-(***), hence the branch cycle lemma and Riemann existence
proofSteps: Choose t_0 and a bouquet (gamma_1, ..., gamma_r) for P^1(C) - t, and phi : pi_1(P^1 - t)_{Qbar} -> G with phi(x_i) = g_i (Riemann existence).
For tau in G_Q, (*), (**), (***) and (H2) put (phi(x_1^tau), ..., phi(x_r^tau)) in sni(C_1, ..., C_r).
By (H3) there is varphi_tau with (phi(x_i^tau)) = varphi_tau (g_i) varphi_tau^{-1}.
By (H1) varphi_tau is unique, so tau -> varphi_tau is a homomorphism, and 8.1.2 gives descent to Q; regularity holds because the cover is defined over Qbar with group G.
acceptance: IG.3 acceptance: one rigid realization (S_n or PSL_2(F_p), see the examples node) with the conjugacy classes, centralizers and rationality checked.

nodes.title: Debes Propositions 8.4.1-8.4.4, Remarque 8.4.5, Corollaire 8.4.6 and Romagny-Wewers Theorem 4.3, Proposition 4.4: the field of moduli, when it is a field of definition, and the obstruction in H^2(k_m, Z(G))
nodes.statement: For a (G-)extension E/F(T) with F/k Galois, M(E) is the subgroup of tau in Gal(F/k) with E^tau isomorphic to E, and its fixed field is the field of moduli. It is a finite extension of k contained in every field of definition containing k (8.4.1), and M(E) is closed. Over F = k^s with t_0 in P^1(k) - t, the field of moduli is a field of definition iff the induced homomorphism G_k -> N/C lifts to G_k -> N, with N = Nor_R(G) and C = Cen_R(G) (8.4.4). This holds when C = 1 (in particular for G-covers of center-free G, and mere covers without automorphisms), for Galois extensions viewed as mere covers (Coombes-Harbater), for abelian G, and whenever G_k is projective (k finite, cd k <= 1). The field R_{t0}(E) fixed by the kernel is a field of definition of degree <= |N|/|C| (8.4.6). For tame G-covers over an algebraically closed field, the field of moduli is a finite separable extension of the branch-locus field (Romagny-Wewers Theorem 4.3; tameness is necessary). In general the obstruction for the field of moduli to be a field of definition lies in H^2(k_m, Z_G) (Romagny-Wewers, citing Debes-Douai 1997).

proofSteps: 8.4.1: a field of definition K has Gal(F/K) contained in M(E); the orbit map tau -> (phi(x_i^tau)) mod N shows [k_m : k] is finite.
8.4.3: tau in M(E) iff there is varphi_tau in N with phi(x^{s(tau)}) = varphi_tau phi(x) varphi_tau^{-1}; k_m is a field of definition iff the varphi_tau can be chosen to form a homomorphism.

8.4.4: the classes varphi_tau mod C form a homomorphism G_k -> N/C; lifting is possible if 1 -> C -> N -> N/C -> 1 splits (C = 1, abelian G, Galois mere covers via the regular representation) or G_k is projective.

nodes.statement: An embedding problem E(G, phi, alpha) for a profinite group G is a diagram with exact sequence 1 -> N -> E -alpha-> Gbar -> 1 of profinite groups and a surjection phi : G -> Gbar. nodes.statement: Let K/k be a finite Galois extension of a global field with G = Gal(K/k) and phi : G_k -> G. nodes.title: Romagny-Wewers Theorem 2.1, Corollary 2.2, Theorem 4.11 and Debes 2026 Theorem 2.4: the Hurwitz space H_{r,G} of tame G-covers of P^1 with r branch points over Z, fine when Z(G) = 1, with good reduction and compactification away from |G|
nodes.statement: For a finite group G and r >= 3 there is a scheme H = H_{r,G,Z}, smooth of finite type over Z, with a morphism of functors from isomorphism classes of tame G-covers of P^1_S with r branch points to Hom(S, H), universal among such morphisms and bijective for S the spectrum of an algebraically closed field (Theorem 2.1). If Z(G) = 1 it is a fine moduli space (Corollary 2.2), so for every field k its k-points are the regular tame G-extensions of k(t). The algebraic construction gives H of finite type over Z with an etale map pi : H -> U_{r,Z} to the configuration space, compatible with twisting by field automorphisms ([f^sigma] = [f]^sigma), so the field of moduli of f is the residue field of its point, and H (x) C = H_{r,G,C} (Theorem 4.11). Over Z[1/|G|] it is smooth with a normal compactification over the Harris-Mumford compactification of the configuration space, its reductions at p not dividing |G| are moduli spaces for G-covers in characteristic p (Debes 2026 Theorem 2.4, citing Wewers and Romagny-Wewers). Reduced Hurwitz spaces (quotients by PGL_2) are normal but not necessarily smooth over Z.

nodes.statement: The branch-locus map Psi_r : H_{r,G,C} -> U_{r,C} is a covering projection and H_{r,G,C} has a unique complex structure making Psi_r locally biholomorphic. As a covering it is determined by the action of pi_1(U_{r,C}) (the Hurwitz braid group) on the fibre ni_r(G); the connected components of H_{r,G,C} correspond to the braid orbits on ni_r(G). With Riemann existence this gives, for suitable r and G, components defined over Q: Debes 2026 Theorem 2.1 states that for every finite group G there are r and a component of Hur_{r,G} defined over Q with real points (resp. Q_p-points), whence (Corollary 2.2) every finite group is the group of a regular Galois extension of k(T) with a totally k-rational fibre for k = Q^tr or Q^tp.
